sources.citation: Jordan, Linda. 2015. A Comparison of Five Speech Varieties of Southwestern Angola: Comparing OluHumbe, OluCilenge, OluKwandu, OluNgendelengo, and OluKuvale in the Kamucuio Municipality, Namibe Province. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-017. Dallas: SIL International. iii+29 pp. (SIL archive entry 64363; PDF downloaded via the Internet Archive capture of the sil.org reapdata URL)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Survey report: lexicostatistics, noun classes, segmental sound correspondences (sec. 4.3) and wordlists (only the first 200 items elicited in OluNgendelengo). Sec. 4.3, p. 7: 'Tone is not covered in this paper in order to focus on the segmental correspondences.' No stress/accent statement; transcriptions carry no prosodic marks.

sources.note: Only modern linguistic treatment of the Kuvale cluster (Ngendelengo's closest relative per ISO CR 2016-036); reports phoneme inventories of surveyed SW-Angolan Herero/Kuvale varieties and may include or comment on Ngendelengo and on prosody (tone vs. stress). Would at best be a statement about the cluster, not a dedicated Ngendelengo description.
